d: The small, hardy, infectious form of Chlamydia that survives outside cells and enters epithelium by endocytosis, then converts into the replicating reticulate body inside a vacuole.

Pain when the cervix is moved during a bimanual exam, because the movement stretches an inflamed uterus, tubes and pelvic peritoneum; the classic bedside sign of pelvic inflammatory disease, also called the chandelier sign.

Perihepatitis from PID organisms that track up the right paracolic gutter to the liver capsule, causing right upper quadrant pain and violin-string adhesions between the capsule and the abdominal wall.

The VDRL or RPR, which detects antibody to cardiolipin, reports a titer that falls after successful treatment, and can be falsely positive in lupus, antiphospholipid syndrome, pregnancy and viral infections.
Giving a patient treated for chlamydia or gonorrhea a prescription or medication for a sex partner who has not been examined, legal in most states because it reduces reinfection.

A pyosalpinx is a fallopian tube distended with pus because the infected fimbriated end has sealed; it can become a tubo-ovarian abscess. A hydrosalpinx is a scarred, sealed tube filled with clear fluid, the healed end stage that causes tubal factor infertility.
